# sigma_connection (Resource)

A Sigma data connection.

**Credentials in `details_json` are write-only.** They are sent to Sigma on create/update but never read back — the API strips them from GET responses.

**Importing an existing connection:** `details_json` cannot be recovered from the server. After import, the next plan will propose to re-PATCH `details_json` with the value from your config (this is harmless if you have the credentials, since the PATCH just re-sends them). To suppress that diff, add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [details_json] }` to the imported resource.

**Snowflake host/account/server quirk:** despite Sigma's OpenAPI listing `host`, `account`, and `server` as interchangeable, in practice for Snowflake the canonical field is `account` and Sigma appends `.snowflakecomputing.com` server-side. Pass the raw `<orgname>-<accountname>` form (no FQDN suffix) — passing the FQDN double-appends and fails with `Could not connect to host`. `server` works as a synonym for `account`; `host` is rejected.

**Azure SQL DB / SQL Server is not currently API-manageable.** Sigma's UI distinguishes `Azure SQL DB` (EngineEdition 5) from `SQL Server 2022` (EngineEditions 1–4 with ProductMajorVersion 16.x, or 8 for Managed Instance) as two distinct connection types, but the public REST API exposes only `type: "sqlserver"`. Posting to `/v2/connections` with this type returns `Could not connect to database` even with valid creds and an open firewall — Sigma's API is likely routing the request to the SQL Server 2022 driver regardless of the target's EngineEdition. Tracked at SIG-99778. Workaround: create SQL Server connections in the Sigma UI; this provider can manage everything else (members, teams, grants on those connections, etc.) while the API gap is closed.

**Starburst / Trino / Presto is not exposed by Sigma's public REST API.** Despite UI support, `POST /v2/connections` rejects these type values at schema validation. Tracked at SIG-99778.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# See Sigma's docs for the full per-warehouse `details` schema:
# https://help.sigmacomputing.com/reference/createconnection
#
# Snowflake gotcha: `account` should be the raw `<orgname>-<accountname>` form
# (no `.snowflakecomputing.com` suffix — Sigma appends it server-side). Passing
# the FQDN double-appends and the create returns 400 "Could not connect to host".
# `server` is accepted as a synonym for `account`. `host` is NOT — despite the  
# OpenAPI oneOf treating them as interchangeable, Snowflake-typed connections
# reject `host`.
resource "sigma_connection" "warehouse" {
  name = "primary-warehouse"

  details_json = jsonencode({
    type      = "snowflake"
    account   = "MYORG-MYACCOUNT" # raw, no FQDN
    user      = "SIGMA_SVC"
    password  = var.snowflake_password
    warehouse = "ANALYTICS_WH"
    role      = "SIGMA_ROLE"
  })

  # If you ever `terraform import` this resource, uncomment the lifecycle
  # block below — Sigma's GET strips credentials, so the next plan would
  # otherwise propose a re-PATCH of details_json.
  # lifecycle {
  #   ignore_changes = [details_json]
  # }
}

variable "snowflake_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Snowflake key-pair auth example (verified end-to-end in stress test):
#
# resource "sigma_connection" "warehouse_kp" {
#   name = "primary-warehouse-kp"
#   details_json = jsonencode({
#     type       = "snowflake"
#     authType   = "key-pair"
#     account    = "MYORG-MYACCOUNT"
#     user       = "SIGMA_SVC"
#     privateKey = var.snowflake_private_key  # PEM-encoded, including BEGIN/END lines
#   })
# }

# Grant a team usage permission on the entire connection.
resource "sigma_connection_grant" "analytics_uses_warehouse" {
  connection_id = sigma_connection.warehouse.id
  team_id       = sigma_team.analytics.id
  permission    = "usage"
}

# Or grant on a specific schema (path).
data "sigma_connection_path" "raw_orders" {
  connection_id = sigma_connection.warehouse.id
  path          = "ANALYTICS_DB.RAW.ORDERS"
}

resource "sigma_connection_path_grant" "raw_orders_team_usage" {
  connection_path_id = data.sigma_connection_path.raw_orders.connection_path_id
  team_id            = sigma_team.analytics.id
  permission         = "usage"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `details_json` (String, Sensitive) JSON-encoded connection details object per Sigma's POST /v2/connections oneOf schema. Write-only: never returned by GET, so refresh leaves the state value unchanged (no drift detection on this field). For Snowflake, set `account` to the raw `<orgname>-<accountname>` (Sigma appends `.snowflakecomputing.com`). For Snowflake OAuth connections, set `roleSwitching` (`allRoles` or `disabled`) inside this blob to control whether users may switch roles when running queries; the configured value is surfaced read-only on `role_switching`.
- `name` (String) Connection name.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `is_audit_log` (Boolean)
- `is_sample` (Boolean)
- `oauth_client_id` (String) OAuth client ID configured on this connection, if any. Read-only (not part of the create body).
- `oauth_jwk_set_id` (String) JWK set signing JWT bearer assertions for this connection, if any. Read-only — set it via `jwkSetId` (with `useJwt = true`) inside `details_json`.
- `organization_id` (String)
- `role_switching` (String) For Snowflake OAuth connections, whether users may switch roles when running queries (`allRoles` or `disabled`). Read-only — set it via `roleSwitching` inside `details_json`. Empty for non-Snowflake-OAuth connections.
- `type` (String) Warehouse type (e.g. `postgres`, `snowflake`, `bigQuery`). Derived from `details_json.type`.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `use_oauth` (Boolean)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sigma_connection.example '<connection_id>'
```
